title: Upgrading to 0.22: LLM Framework Transition

book.title: NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails Library Developer Guide

description: How NeMo Guardrails 0.22 routes engines through the new DefaultFramework, when LangChain is still required, and how to opt in.
content:
Upgrading to 0.22: LLM Framework Transition NeMo Guardrails 0.22 introduces a DefaultFramework that talks to OpenAI-compatible endpoints directly over httpx , with no LangChain dependency on the request path. As a result, langchain and the provider-specific langchain-* packages are now development-only dependencies of nemoguardrails . The guiding principle is: Prefer DefaultFramework whenever the underlying wire protocol is OpenAI-compatible. Use LangChain only as the fallback for engines whose API is not OpenAI-compatible. This guide explains how the routing works, when you need to install LangChain, how to migrate legacy engine: vllm_openai configs, and how to control the active framework. Your existing config keeps working If your config.yml uses one of the four engines below, the upgrade is silent: the same pip install nemoguardrails install pulls everything you need, and your config does not change. Engine Default base URL openai https://api.openai.com/v1 nim https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 nvidia_ai_endpoints https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 (alias for nim ) ollama http://localhost:11434/v1 These engines are routed to DefaultFramework , which builds an OpenAIChatModel against an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint. You can override the endpoint by setting parameters.base_url and the API key by setting parameters.api_key (or the engine-specific environment variable, for example OPENAI_API_KEY , NVIDIA_API_KEY ). models
type: main
engine: nim
model: meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct
parameters
temperature: 0.0
max_tokens: 1024
No code change, no new install command. OpenAI-compatible self-hosted and third-party endpoints Many providers expose an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions route. For all of them, the recommended migration is: Use engine: openai plus parameters.base_url . Do not use engine: vllm_openai and do not set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain . Examples that fall under this pattern: vLLM with the OpenAI-compatible API ( python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server ). TGI / Hugging Face TEI when deployed with /v1/chat/completions enabled. OpenRouter at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 . Together.ai , Fireworks.ai , Groq . DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/v1 . llama.cpp server with --api . Any other “OpenAI-compatible” self-hosted endpoint. Migrating a legacy vllm_openai config If your old config looked like this: models
type: main
engine: vllm_openai
model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
parameters
openai_api_base: http://localhost:5000/v1
Migrate to: models
type: main
engine: openai
model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
parameters
base_url: http://localhost:5000/v1
api_key: EMPTY
When self-hosted vLLM does not enforce authentication, set parameters.api_key to any non-empty placeholder such as EMPTY . If your deployment requires a real token, replace it with that value or load it through api_key_env_var . The legacy engine: vllm_openai form is still recognized by the LangChain framework, but for new configurations the DefaultFramework form above is preferred. When you need LangChain Engines whose API is not OpenAI-compatible still require LangChain. To use them you must: Install LangChain plus the provider-specific package yourself. Either set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain for the whole process, or use engine: langchain/<provider> in config.yml . Examples that genuinely need LangChain: vertexai (Google Vertex AI). anthropic (Anthropic Claude). cohere . azure (Azure OpenAI uses a deployment-name URL plus api-version query string that the DefaultFramework’s OpenAI-compatible client does not currently support). huggingface_pipeline / hf_pipeline_* (in-process Python pipeline). huggingface_hub . huggingface_endpoint (default text-generation schema; if your endpoint exposes /v1/chat/completions , prefer the DefaultFramework engine: openai plus parameters.base_url instead). trt_llm (TensorRT-LLM in-process). self_hosted (LangChain self-hosted wrapper). Install command pip install langchain langchain-<provider
For example, to use Anthropic Claude: pip install langchain langchain-anthropic
For Cohere: pip install langchain langchain-cohere
For Azure OpenAI: pip install langchain langchain-openai
The provider package list is the same as the LangChain integration list. See the LangChain chat-model integrations page for the full set of community providers. Using engine: langchain Once LangChain and the provider package are installed, point your config.yml at the LangChain framework: models
type: main
engine: langchain/anthropic
model: claude-3-5-sonnet-latest
parameters
temperature: 0.0
engine: langchain/<provider> tells the registry to use LangChainFramework and to instantiate the provider’s LangChain chat model with the keys under parameters . If you previously used engine: anthropic or engine: cohere directly, that path now requires NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain . Set the variable globally for the process or migrate to the langchain/<provider> form. Choosing the active framework NeMo Guardrails resolves the framework name in two places: The NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK environment variable, read once when the framework registry initializes. The default value is default . The set_default_framework(name) function, which mutates the registry at runtime. Environment variable Set NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK before starting the process: export NEMOGUARDRAILS_LLM_FRAMEWORK=langchain
nemoguardrails chat --config=path/to/config
Accepted values: default (default) - the new httpx-based path. Engines openai , nim , nvidia_ai_endpoints , ollama , plus any other OpenAI-compatible provider configured with engine: openai and parameters.base_url . langchain - all engine resolutions go through LangChainFramework . Useful when every model in your config is a LangChain provider. Any name you have registered yourself with register_framework(name, instance) . Programmatic switch from nemoguardrails import set_default_framework
set_default_framework("langchain
set_default_framework raises KeyError if the name has not been registered and is not one of the lazy-loaded built-ins ( default , langchain ). Registering a custom framework from nemoguardrails import register_framework, set_default_framework
from my_pkg import MyFramework
register_framework("my-framework", MyFramework
set_default_framework("my-framework
register_framework raises ValueError if a framework with the same name is already registered. Common errors “No default base_url for provider ‘X’” ValueError: No default base_url for provider 'cohere
Set it explicitly in model parameters: parameters.base_url
This error comes from _resolve_base_url in nemoguardrails/llm/frameworks/default.py . It means the engine name you used (here cohere ) is not in DefaultFramework ’s routing table and is not an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Fix: either supply a parameters.base_url for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or switch to the LangChain framework with engine: langchain/cohere and install langchain-cohere . “Framework ‘X’ is already registered” register_framework does not allow rebinding. Either pick a different name or, in tests, call the registry-reset hook before re-registering. “Unknown framework ‘X’” set_default_framework was called with a name that is not registered and is not one of the lazy built-ins default or langchain . Register the framework first, or correct the name. Provider matrix and supported LLMs For the full engine-to-framework matrix, including streaming and tool-calling support per engine, see the Routing matrix in Supported LLMs . Related references Configuration YAML Schema Reference - all models.* fields, including parameters semantics for both frameworks. LangChain Integration - using RunnableRails , agent middleware, and chains as actions. Custom LLM Providers - registering a provider inside a framework
summary: NeMo Guardrails 0.22 introduces a DefaultFramework that talks to OpenAI-compatible endpoints directly over httpx, with no LangChain dependency on the request path. As a result, langchain and the provider-specific langchain-* packages are now development-only dependencies of nemoguardrails.
